title_en: Chen Kaihua — endangering traffic safety by means of vehicle hijacking
keywords_en: criminal; crime of endangering public security; first instance; second instance; retrial; Basic People's Court; Intermediate People's Court; High People's Court; Fujian Province; natural person; Criminal Law; characterization of conduct; applicability of analogy; determination of charge; reversal of judgment; hijacking a motor vehicle; threat with a firearm; public transportation safety
full_text_en:
Chen Kaihua — Endangering Traffic Safety by Dangerous Means of Hijacking a Motor Vehicle

Defendant: Chen Kaihua, male, 28 years old, farmer from Wuqiao Village, Buwen Township, Longhai County, Fujian Province. Arrested on April 25, 1991.

The People's Procuratorate of Longhai County filed a public prosecution against the defendant Chen Kaihua for the crime of hooliganism, and brought the case before the Longhai County People's Court. The Longhai County People's Court, after public trial, found the following facts:

On the morning of April 7, 1991, the defendant Chen Kaihua, carrying RMB 10,700 in cash, took a bus to Shima Town, Longhai County, to repay a loan to his uncle Chen Shucong. To guard against unforeseen incidents on the road, Chen Kaihua brought with him a homemade火药 gun converted from a sports starting pistol. At around 3:00 p.m. that day, Chen Kaihua, after drinking alcohol, left Chen Shucong's home and boarded a public bus (license plate No. 35-90542) operated by Longhai County Yufa Automobile Transportation Company to return home. At that time, there were over 20 passengers on the bus. Shortly after the bus departed from Shima Town, Chen Kaihua thought of going to Baitu Field in Wuqiao Xukeng Village to find a person named Lin to resolve a dispute over kaolin excavation, and thus conceived the evil idea of hijacking the bus to that village. Thereupon, standing behind the driver, Chen Kaihua drew his homemade gun, aimed it at the back of the driver's head, and commanded: "Drive wherever I tell you, or I'll shoot!" Under the threat of the gun, the driver continued driving. When the bus reached the Xixi area, a passenger wanted to get off; the driver applied the brakes to let the passenger off. Chen Kaihua then threatened the driver: "No more stops!" The bus continued along the National Highway Fu-Zhang route. When it reached the intersection leading to Tianzhai Village, Chen Kaihua ordered the driver to change direction and turn into the small road to Tianzhai Village. Shortly after turning onto the small road, the bus encountered a hand-tractor blocking the way. Chen Kaihua jumped off the bus and told the tractor driver to move aside. The bus continued along the small road and soon encountered a farm cart blocking the way. Seeing this, Chen Kaihua took out RMB 10 from his pocket and gave it to the conductor, saying it was for gasoline, then got off the bus again and told the farm cart driver to make way. The bus driver saw that Chen Kaihua had followed the farm cart to a bend and was some distance from the bus, so he seized the opportunity to turn the bus around and drive away. When Chen Kaihua saw the bus heading in the opposite direction, he did not pursue it. Chen Kaihua then went to Baitu Field but did not find Lin, so he returned home alone. After driving away, the bus driver reported the incident to the local public security authorities.

That evening, upon discovering that public security personnel were pursuing him, defendant Chen Kaihua fled and went into hiding. On the 15th of that month, Chen Kaihua, accompanied by his relatives, surrendered to the public security authorities and handed over the gun used in the crime.

The above facts are confirmed by the report records of the driver and conductor of the hijacked bus, Chen Kaihua's surrender record, the confiscated homemade gun used in the crime, and witness testimony.

The Longhai County People's Court held: The defendant Chen Kaihua knowingly used a gun to threaten the driver, causing severe psychological panic in the driver, which could potentially lead to a traffic accident, yet he adopted an attitude of indifference towards the lives and property safety of the passengers on the bus. By using a gun to hijack a public bus in motion, his conduct endangered public safety and constituted a crime, warranting punishment. The charge of hooliganism brought by the prosecutor was inappropriate. Chen Kaihua's criminal conduct was not explicitly provided for in the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 79 of the Criminal Law, analogy was applied by comparing it to the most similar provision in the Specific Provisions for conviction and sentencing. The object of Chen Kaihua's criminal conduct was a means of transportation, which was most similar to the crime of sabotaging means of transportation provided for in Article 107 of the Criminal Law. Therefore, he should be convicted and sentenced by analogy under that Article. Accordingly, on August 22, 1991, the Longhai County People's Court rendered its judgment: The defendant Chen Kaihua was found guilty of the crime of hijacking a motor vehicle and sentenced to three years' imprisonment.

The defendant Chen Kaihua appealed against the first-instance judgment, arguing that he had voluntarily surrendered and requested a lighter sentence.

After trial, the Zhangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province held: The facts of Chen Kaihua's crime as determined in the first-instance judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the application of legal analogy was correct, and the trial procedures were lawful. The conviction of the defendant Chen Kaihua for the crime of hijacking a motor vehicle was accurate, but the sentence was excessively heavy. Considering that the circumstances of Chen Kaihua's crime were relatively minor and that he surrendered after committing the crime, pursuant to Article 63 of the Criminal Law, a mitigated punishment could be imposed, and his request for a lighter sentence could be accepted. Accordingly, on October 4, 1991, the Zhangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered its judgment: The appellant Chen Kaihua was found guilty of the crime of hijacking a motor vehicle and sentenced to one year and six months' imprisonment. In accordance with the procedures for approving cases involving analogy in the application of law, the Zhangzhou Intermediate People's Court submitted this case to the Fujian High People's Court for review.

After review, the Fujian High People's Court held: The facts determined in the judgment of the Longhai County People's Court, that the defendant Chen Kaihua used a gun and violent coercion to hijack a public bus in operation, were clear, and the evidence was reliable and sufficient. Chen Kaihua's conduct endangered public safety and constituted a crime, warranting punishment according to law. However, the conviction and sentencing under Article 107 of the Criminal Law in the first-instance judgment were improper. For cases involving conviction and sentencing by analogy in the application of law, first, the crime must not be explicitly provided for in the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law; second, conviction and sentencing must be by reference to the most similar provision in the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law. Article 107 of the Criminal Law refers to the intentional sabotage of means of transportation, sufficient to cause the overturning or destruction of such means, thereby endangering traffic safety. Subjectively, Chen Kaihua did not have the intent to sabotage the means of transportation; his hijacking of the bus was not for the purpose of destroying the bus or causing its overturning or destruction to endanger traffic safety, but was merely a means to achieve the goal of riding to Lin's home. Because the subjective aspect of Chen Kaihua's crime did not correspond to that required under Article 107 of the Criminal Law, Article 107 was not the most similar provision to Chen Kaihua's criminal conduct, and thus could not be applied by analogy for conviction and sentencing. Although Chen Kaihua's act of hijacking a motor vehicle technically corresponded to the means of crime under Article 100(3) of the Criminal Law, his conduct lacked a counterrevolutionary purpose, and therefore should not be convicted as the crime of hijacking a motor vehicle under that Article either. From the characteristics of Chen Kaihua's criminal conduct of using a gun and violent coercion to hijack a public bus in operation, his purpose was to ride the bus to find Lin, and he adopted an attitude of indifference towards the lives and property safety of the bus and its passengers. The essence of his conduct was endangering public safety, which was already encompassed within the crime of "endangering public safety by other dangerous means" under Article 105 of the Criminal Law. Therefore, Chen Kaihua's criminal conduct was not a crime not explicitly provided for in the Specific Provisions of the Criminal Law, and analogy was inapplicable; he could be directly convicted and sentenced under Article 105 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, on March 15, 1993, the Fujian High People's Court issued Criminal Order (1992) Min Fa Xing Lei Tui Zi No. 1, quashing the criminal judgments of the Zhangzhou Intermediate People's Court (1991) Zhang Zhong Fa Xing Shang Zi No. 79 and the Longhai County People's Court (1991) No. 089, and remanded the case to the Longhai County People's Court for retrial.

After retrial, the Longhai County People's Court held: The defendant Chen Kaihua, by aiming a homemade gun at the back of the bus driver's head, hijacked a public bus in operation and forcibly ordered it to proceed to a designated location. Although no serious consequences resulted, this conduct was sufficient to threaten the personal and property safety of multiple persons. His conduct constituted the crime of endangering traffic safety by dangerous means of hijacking a motor vehicle. The object infringed upon by Chen Kaihua's conduct was public safety. The charge of hooliganism brought by the Longhai County People's Procuratorate was inappropriate. After the incident, the defendant Chen Kaihua voluntarily surrendered, and the defense counsel's request for a lighter punishment could be accepted. Pursuant to Articles 105, 60, 63, and 59 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Longhai County People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 22, 1993: 1. The defendant Chen Kaihua is guilty of the crime of endangering traffic safety by dangerous means of hijacking a motor vehicle and is sentenced to one year and six months' imprisonment; 2. The instrument of crime, one homemade gun, is confiscated.

After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Chen Kaihua indicated acceptance of the verdict.
